artists.biography:
George Evelyn (also known as Nightmares on Wax or DJ EASE), is a DJ and electronic music composer from Leeds, England. His music is released on Warp Records and was one of the first releases on the label.
Evelyn got his start in the music industry through an interest in hip hop and on joining a local breakdancing crew. He met Kevin Harper and together they released their first album in 1991, a techno-edged record entitled "A Word Of Science: The First And Final Chapter". This was the beginning of NoW's career. Today, Harper is a solo DJ and Evelyn is accompanied by Robin Taylor-Firth.
It is not a coincidence that the name Nightmares on Wax is an acronym for NOW, as they describe their music as "the sound of N.O.W." to exemplify raw honesty and artistic freedom. Evelyn elaborates, "Today's music is inspired by whatever has gone on before. That's what fascinates me. Soul music is the earliest form of hip hop. That's why I want to create it. It might seem like recreating what was done in the past, but what I want to do is merge soul and hip hop together. That's why I'll bring in the live aspect of what happened back then into current hip hop trends. That's the angle I'm arriving at."

perplexity.description:
Smokers Delight, released in 1995 on Warp Records, is the second studio album by Nightmares on Wax and a defining work in the electronic genre. The album blends laid-back trip-hop, dub, soul, and jazz influences, characterized by smooth, sample-based production, mellow beats, and a warm, vintage atmosphere. Tracks like "Nights Introlude" and "Stars" showcase the album's signature sound—relaxed yet intricately layered, evoking a sense of nostalgia and comfort. Its style helped cement Nightmares on Wax as a key figure in the UK's electronic music scene of the mid-1990s.

Within the artist's discography, Smokers Delight stands as a landmark release, following the debut A Word of Science: The 1st and Final Chapter. It expanded on the project's sonic palette, moving further into downtempo and soulful territory, and set the stage for later works like Carboot Soul. The album reached number 84 on the UK Albums Chart and was widely praised for its creativity and timeless quality, often cited as a quintessential chill-out record. Critics and listeners alike have recognized it as a classic of its era, emblematic of the relaxed, introspective mood that defined much of Warp Records' output in the 1990s.
